top_stories.title: They are not illegal aliens: 12 Indians involved with 'criminal tourism' in Canada, they came to steal - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Durham regional police** arrested 46 individuals, including those from India and Romania, in connection with what they are calling "criminal tourism," where international organized crime groups send people to Canada for high-profit crimes. The investigation, **Project Jetsetter**, has led to over 200 incidents since 2019 resulting in $2.6 million in financial losses and 1,500 charges.  The suspects are accused of engaging in a range of criminal activities including retail theft, vehicle purchasing scams, jewelry theft, and insurance fraud. **RCMP National Intelligence** director general Mario Panizzon stated that this activity is borderless and impacts Canadians daily.

top_stories.title: Trump administration launches largest-ever push to revoke citizenship of 17 people accused of fraud, including one Indian - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: The **Trump administration** is set to announce a major escalation in its immigration crackdown, targeting 17 naturalized US citizens accused of various crimes including sexual offenses and financial misconduct. The move marks the largest-ever use of US denaturalisation powers, allowing the government to strip citizenship from individuals who obtained it through fraud or concealment.  The **Justice Department** will pursue these cases aggressively, with Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche stating that "criminal aliens are lying about their past crimes." Those facing denaturalization can challenge the government's case in court.

top_stories.title: INDIA bloc in disarray, lacks ground presence: BJP - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: The **Bharatiya Janata Party** (BJP) criticized the **Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance** (INDIA), claiming it is disintegrating due to internal conflicts and electoral losses. The BJP, meanwhile, emphasized its focus on public trust through welfare programs and India's development by 2047.

top_stories.title: Trump’s Middle East peace remains under construction and Israel and Iran shoot at each other - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **President Donald Trump** is attempting to maintain a fragile ceasefire between **Israel** and **Iran**, despite renewed missile exchanges and escalating mistrust.  He insists that a broader peace agreement is within reach, but negotiations remain stalled due to disagreements over sanctions relief and the unfreezing of Iranian assets.  The president's optimistic rhetoric contrasts with the reality on the ground as military exchanges continue across the region.  **Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu** and other Iran hawks remain skeptical of Trump's approach.

top_stories.title: Chhagan Bhujbal sidelined, NCP’s Rajendra Jain files nomination for Rajya Sabha - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Rajendra Jain**, former **NCP** MLC, filed his nomination as the party's candidate for the upcoming Rajya Sabha by-election in Maharashtra. The by-poll is scheduled for June 18th and follows Deputy Chief Minister **Sunetra Pawar's** resignation.  **Pawar** chose **Jain** over senior Cabinet Minister and OBC leader **Chhagan Bhujbal**, who had expressed interest in both a Rajya Sabha seat and a ministerial position for his nephew, **Sameer Bhujbal**.

top_stories.title: 'No visa laws that target India': What US official recently said on H-1B woes - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **The State Department** has defended the recent changes to H-1B visa rules, stating they are global and not targeted at **India**.  Spokesperson Tommy Pigott clarified that these new regulations aim for consistent application of visa law across all countries. He emphasized that while facilitating entry for skilled workers is important, ensuring opportunities for American citizens remains a priority. The changes have led to significant delays in visa stamping renewals, particularly for Indian H-1B holders who must now renew their visas in their home countries.

top_stories.title: House pattas will be given to eligible SC/ST families within 5 years: Minister Vanni Arasu - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Minister for Social Justice Vanni Arasu** stated that the government aims to provide house pattas to all eligible SC/ST families within five years. He emphasized this initiative as a top priority, and plans to implement it after consultations with **Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay**.  The minister also highlighted his commitment to addressing caste-based conflicts in schools and colleges, reviewing police station transfers, and improving the conditions of SC/ST hostels and schools.

top_stories.title: 'No visa laws that target India': What US official recently said on H-1B woes - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **The State Department** has stated that the recent changes to H-1B visa rules, requiring stamping in home countries and social media vetting, are not targeted at **India**.  Spokesperson Tommy Pigott clarified that these are global visa laws being implemented consistently across all applicants. He emphasized that the US prioritizes facilitating investment and worker training while ensuring opportunities for American citizens.
